# Study 1 reanalysis (generated by `src/rt/study1.py`; numbers in `study1.json`)

Lexical scoring of `src/metrics.py`; bootstrap 10,000 case resamples, seed 42, percentile 95% CI, two-sided p = 2·min(#≤0, #≥0)/B, cases resampled in sorted case_id order. Llama-70B is shown unfiltered (n=200) and under `score_pilot.py --drop-degenerate` (n=187).

## 4 Sampling reliability (Qwen-32B, 3 seeds, T=0.6)

Among 124 edits with greedy ES@B0: at least one of 3 sampled B3 answers fails 0.605 [0.516, 0.694]; the same over 3 sampled B0 answers (noise floor) 0.339 [0.258, 0.427]; excess 0.266 [0.169, 0.363] (p=0.0000).

158 of 171 checks match (results.json six headline cells and REVISION.md §2).

| Holm ES drop Llama-70B raw p | p | 0.0024 | 0.0036 |
| Holm ES drop Qwen-32B raw p | p | 0.0082 | 0.0066 |
| retention Qwen-14B CI low | ci | 0.057 | 0.069 |
| qualified ES drop Qwen-32B CI low | ci | 0.04 | 0.0329 |
| arm T-P ES point | point | 0.122 | 0.1212 |

Note: bootstrap-sequence dependent, point estimate matches: REVISION.md §2 came from an exploratory pass that resampled cases in shard-file order (random.Random(42); numpy default_rng(42) for the qualified CIs); study1 resamples in sorted case_id order as cross_arm does. Replaying the exploratory convention on the same per-case values returns the target exactly.
Note: results.json sup_battery counts P n=199 and was computed from an earlier state of the P shards; the local P shards hold 200 B3 cases and reproduce results 2/esup_crossarm.json exactly; dropping any one of the four OOM-retried P cases does not recover the results.json values
